research_question: Which single mutants of the 44-residue SDA sequence are most likely to show high measured fitness?
control_variables: per-position single masking (identical to entry-function semantics)
execution_evidence: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 code/score_all.py scores.json` (imports the asset entry module /data/mzb/paper2agent/model_assets/esm2_variant/infer.py and calls _residue_logprobs per position). Output scores.json: 834 scores. Reproducibility check vs shipped examples.json: A16C entry=-6.815323 mine=-6.815323 (diff 0.0), A16D entry=-9.651920 mine=-9.651920 (diff 0.0). Cross-check via sanctioned run_model: T17R 1.024920 (mine 1.024919), T17M 0.152818 (mine 0.152818), T17V 1.941504 (mine 1.941504).
uncertainty: Delta log-likelihood is dimensionless and not on a fitness scale; masked-marginal approximation; no structure/ligand context.
conclusion: ESM-2 zero-shot scores were computed for all 834 single mutants; the ranking is dominated by position-17, position-14, 37, 40 and 22 substitutions. These are MODEL PREDICTIONS (E1), not measurements.
limitations: zero-shot ranking quality is protein- and assay-specific
ESM-2 does not separate stability from function
scores are not calibrated to the DMS fitness scale.

research_question: What are the measured fitness values of the top ESM-2-ranked and hotspot mutants, and do they support ranking by ESM-2?
model: hidden evidence oracle (ProteinGym v1 DMS: SDA_BACSU_Tsuboyama_2023_1PV0)

input_data.selection_basis: ESM-2 top ranks plus full position-17 sweep and one low-score control

control_variables: same wild-type sequence and assay (ProteinGym v1 DMS, SDA_BACSU_Tsuboyama_2023_1PV0)
uncertainty: n=16; sampling is ESM-2-biased and clustered at position 17; measured differences among the top five (~0.09 span) are small relative to assay noise.
conclusion: All 16 oracle measurements are positive-to-mildly-negative except L9D. The five highest measured values are all position-17 variants: T17R 0.485 > T17K 0.393 > T17I 0.354 > T17V 0.289 > T17M 0.272. Next best measured mutant outside position 17 is S37K at 0.173.
limitations: 13 position-17 variants (e.g. T17Q, T17E, T17N, T17S) and most non-position-17 candidates remain UNOBSERVABLE. Measurements come from one historical DMS/assay and are not re-measured here. Selection of which mutants to query was ESM-2-driven, so the measured subset is biased toward high-ESM candidates and cannot support an unbiased correlation estimate.

research_question: Is ESM-2 zero-shot score predictive enough to identify the 5 highest-fitness mutants on its own?
model: derived analysis over ESM-2 (E1) and oracle (E3)
control_variables: analysis script code/analyze.py (python3 -I) using scipy spearmanr
execution_evidence: `python3 code/analyze.py` wrote analysis.json: spearman_all16=0.147 (p=0.587), pearson_all16=0.911, spearman_no_L9D=-0.036 (p=0.899), esm_top5=[T17K,F14K,S37N,H40K,T17I], measured_top5=[T17R,T17K,T17I,T17V,T17M], overlap=2, frac_pos17_measured_above_0.25=0.833.
uncertainty: Small biased sample; ESM-2 within-top ordering unreliable; positional hotspot (pos 17) only discovered through measurement.
conclusion: ESM-2 ranks all 834 mutants but its top-region ordering is not predictive of measured fitness (Spearman rho=-0.036 over the 15 non-extreme measured mutants, p=0.90; only 2/5 of the ESM-2 top-5 appear in the measured top-5). The dominant real signal is positional: position 17 is a permissive hotspot (5/6 measured position-17 mutants exceed 0.25 fitness and occupy the top-5). Final selection therefore prioritizes measured E3 values.
limitations: n=15 non-extreme measurements is tiny and selection-biased toward high-ESM and position-17 mutants, so the rho estimate is noisy and cannot be generalized
the Pearson r=0.911 is driven by the single L9D extreme and does not indicate good within-top discrimination.
